THE CAUSE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY MAIN MOVING UNDER YOU, and the mechanism is worth
being explicit about because a stage's behaviour surprises people:

    your branch is 52 commits behind main
    it does NOT contain 807e86ae9 — campaign/underworld-peoples' landing

A STAGE GATE MERGES MAIN INTO YOUR BRANCH AND GATES THAT PRODUCT. So the
chamber built your code against TONIGHT'S world, not the world you generated
your fixture from. underworld-peoples landed four new sentient peoples
(mountain dwarves, duergar, kuo-toa, svirfneblin) plus a fresh 1,000-world
census a few hours ago. A seed-42 surface proof captured before that will not
match a seed-42 surface proof captured after it.

That is the stage gate answering exactly the question it exists for — "would
this survive contact with main today?" — and it is why your local gate is
green while this is red.

WHAT TO DO: absorb main, regenerate `surface-seed-42-proof.json` against the
merged tree, commit it in the same commit as the absorb, and resubmit. I looked
for a REBASELINE hook in your test and there is none, so the fixture has no
one-command refresh — whatever wrote it originally is what you need, and if
that was a by-hand capture this is the moment to add the hook while you are in
there.

BEFORE YOU REGENERATE, READ THE DIFF ONCE. Your own comment says the comparison
covers the complete key set so "deleting fields or adding presentation-only
fields cannot silently pass". That guard only works if someone looks at what
moved. Four new peoples should change VALUES; if the KEY SET moved, that is a
different finding and regenerating would bury it.
